meta.title: Lawn Mowing in Davison, MI | Grand Scapes
meta.description: Weekly lawn mowing in Davison, MI from Grand Scapes: mowed, trimmed, edged and blown off, on compact city lots and on big township yards, in clean stripes.

hero.title: We mow city lots and **township acres.**
hero.lede: Grand Scapes mows Davison lawns every week: cut, trimmed, edged along the curb and the walk, and blown off before we leave. A small lot near downtown and two acres out in the township both get finished in clean stripes.

local.title: How city and township **lawns differ.**
local.intro: Inside the city, lawns are compact, with a sidewalk or a curb on at least one side, so the edging shows as much as the cut. Out in Davison Township, zoning allows anything from estate lots of an acre and a half to 10 acre parcels, and the mowing is the long part of the visit. Under both sits heavy soil that holds water.

points.title: Edges on a city lot
points.body: On a small lot, a crisp line along the walk and the curb does most of the work. We edge those hard lines every visit, string trim around the fence and the mailbox post, and blow the clippings off the concrete.

points.title: Room to stripe in the township
points.body: On a big township yard, a zero turn covers the open ground quickly. We pick a pattern, straight, curved or crosshatch, and keep the lines running true across the whole lawn from week to week.

points.title: Soft loam after rain
points.body: Much of the city and parts of the township sit on soil that drains slowly. After a soaking rain we skip the softest spots rather than leave tire tracks in them.

points.title: The city's six inch rule
points.body: The city counts grass over six inches on average as a nuisance on lots under an acre. A weekly cut keeps you well clear of it, even in a fast May.

points.title: A third of the blade at a time
points.body: MSU Extension advises taking no more than a third of the grass blade in one mowing, and 2.5 to 3.5 inches suits most lawns. We set the deck in that range so the turf stays thick.

logistics.title: Your weekly mowing day in Davison.
body: Once you say yes, the lawn goes on our weekly route with a set day. It is about 20 minutes from our shop on Embury Road. When a downpour soaks the ground, we shift the cut instead of mowing mud into the lawn, and Rob lets you know by text.

City lots usually mean the truck and trailer at the curb, so we keep the street side tidy and the sidewalk clear for the neighbors. On township acreage, tell us about gates, dogs and soft ground near a ditch, and we plan the route around them.

faq.q: Do you mow lawns in Davison, MI?
faq.a: Yes. Grand Scapes mows lawns every week in the City of Davison and in Davison Township. Each visit is mowed, trimmed, edged and blown off, and Rob gives you a free estimate after he has seen the lawn.

faq.q: How tall can grass get in the City of Davison?
faq.a: Six inches on average, on lots under one acre; past that, the city's ordinance treats grass or rank vegetation as a nuisance. On larger unplatted lots, the strip within 50 feet of the street or a property line has to stay under that height. Weekly mowing handles it.

faq.q: Do you mow big lots in Davison Township?
faq.a: Yes. Township lots can run from an acre and a half to farm parcels of 10 acres or more, and big lawns are a normal part of our week. One of our Google reviews comes from a customer whose 7 1/2 acre lawn we keep all year.

faq.q: How often should a lawn be mowed in Michigan?
faq.a: Weekly through most of the season. MSU Extension says not to remove more than a third of the blade in one mowing, and in a fast spring that can mean more than one cut a week. A weekly visit keeps most lawns inside that rule.

faq.q: What else can you do for a yard in Davison?
faq.a: [Spring cleanups](/spring-cleanup-davison-mi/), [fall leaf removal](/leaf-removal-davison-mi/), [shrub trimming](/shrub-trimming-davison-mi/) and [mulch and beds](/mulch-installation-davison-mi/) all fit around the mowing. Lawn treatments are not on our list, so the weekly visit is about the cut, the trim and the edge.
